newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's Klima says Creditanstalt bid too vague.
newsitem.headline: Austria's Klima says Creditanstalt bid too vague.

text.p: Austrian Finance Minister Viktor Klima on Sunday said an eleventh-hour bid for privatisation candidate Creditanstalt submitted by a group around Austro-Italian insurer EA-Generali was too vague.

The minister, in charge of what has become Austria's longest-running privatisation, said he wanted to see more information on how many of the government's 19.9 million ordinary shares in the bank each of the consortium partners would acquire.
"I have asked for this information to be submitted immediately," Austrian news agency APA quoted Klima as saying.

The consortium, which includes Germany's Commerzbank, Italy's Banca Commercialie Italiana and several smaller Austrian companies, on Friday submitted an offer for Creditanstalt-Bankverein, just hours before a government deadline expired.

It said it would update a proposal it originally made last October, when the group offered to pay nine billion schillings for about two-thirds of the government's 70 percent voting stake in the bank and sell the remaining shares in a secondary offering.
Austrian newspapers over the weekend said the consortium in its latest bid had offered no more than seven billion schillings for the entire stake. No details of the bid have been made public.
Klima has threatened to reopen the bidding process to other potential buyers if the consortium's offer failed to meet his demands. -- Knut Engelmann, Vienna newsroom +431 53112 274
